title: Does a Deterministic Verifier Reduce Unsafe LLM Configuration Applies? A Paired, Emulation‑Grounded Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, emulation‑grounded experiment (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) that measured the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded − baseline) for an LLM‑based network‑configuration pipeline with and without a deterministic verifier. Execution used declared_model = gpt-5-mini, adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial LLM generation per task reused across arms), and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for guarded validation (up to one validator‑triggered repair permitted). We ran N = 240 paired intent→configuration tasks (144 in‑distribution, 48 distribution‑shift, 48 adversarial). All archived scoring artifacts record 'success' as safe; archived analysis reports baseline_success_count = 240 and guarded_success_count = 240. The paired contingency is n11 = 240, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired estimator (guarded_unsafe_rate − baseline_unsafe_rate) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the single shared initial candidate passed deterministic validation in every task and no validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair_attempts = 0), producing a degenerate paired contrast. We present the preregistered design, explicit mapping between estimand and archived analysis outputs, an artifact‑grounded failure analysis of the null paired outcome, and concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for future informative GVR evaluations.

sections.introduction:
Automating the translation of high‑level operator intent into device configurations is a central NetOps goal. Modern LLMs and agentic tool‑use workflows can produce readable configuration sequences, but syntactic fidelity alone does not guarantee safety when changes must satisfy ordering, dependency, and transient invariants in multi‑device network state. Emulation‑grounded, closed‑loop evaluation—where generated configurations are executed against device images/simulators and deterministically scored—reveals semantic failure modes (ordering mistakes, transient violations, protected‑resource touches) not visible in text‑only tests [1].

A widely proposed mitigation is the generate–validate–repair (GVR) pattern: an LLM generates a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks semantic invariants; and an automated repair routine rewrites the candidate when violations are detected [2,3]. Prior work documents the promise of GVR for many syntactic faults but leaves open empirical questions about verifier benefit under distribution shift and adversarial prompts, and about experimental designs that can reliably expose paired differences between guarded and unguarded pipelines [2,4,6].

This paper reports a fully preregistered paired experiment executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics and emulation‑grounded deterministic scoring. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded − baseline). Because the registered adapter produced exactly one initial LLM generation per task reused across both arms, paired differences could arise only when that shared candidate failed validation or when the guarded arm invoked a validator‑triggered repair. We (1) map the preregistered estimand to archived analysis artifacts, (2) report complete execution accounting and exact numeric outcomes from the archived analysis executor, and (3) provide an artifact‑grounded failure analysis explaining why the paired contrast was null and concrete recommendations for future informative GVR studies.
sections.related_work:
Executable, emulation‑grounded NetOps benchmarks place LLM agents in closed‑loop multi‑device networks to surface planning and execution faults beyond token‑level evaluations; NetConfArena is one recent example advocating this evaluation paradigm [1]. Studies of automatic configuration repair and program repair identify generate–validate patterns and show that validators frequently increase repair coverage for many benchmarked faults, while semantic coverage depends strongly on verifier design and the fault taxonomy [2,4]. Survey and position papers synthesize agentic architectures, deterministic tool augmentation, verifier integration, and uncertainty calibration as promising patterns for operational NetOps automation and safety but emphasize gaps in scaling and production validation [3,5]. Engineering precedents such as Batfish illustrate how incremental, static analysis tooling can be applied to configuration semantics and inspire verifier designs [6].

Our study differs from prior work by combining (a) a preregistered paired estimand, (b) preregistered shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, (c) emulation‑grounded deterministic scoring with a declared deterministic verifier, and (d) full archival of per‑call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts so the exact measured estimand and numeric outputs are machine‑reconcilable to archived artifacts. This experimental framing highlights how generation semantics interact with verifier opportunity to produce discordant paired outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand mapping: The experiment was preregistered (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate where unsafe_apply = 1 indicates a final configuration that would cause a semantic safety violation when applied). The archived analysis executor reports 'success' as the safe outcome; we map archived condition_summary and paired_contingency_table fields to the estimand (archived condition_summary shows baseline_success_count = 240 and guarded_success_count = 240; paired_contingency_table shows n11 = 240, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0). Bootstrap parameters (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and exact McNemar test selection are those used by the archived executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1); these analysis parameters are recorded in the archived analysis_log.jsonl.

Design, sampling, and tasks: We used a paired design with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics: exactly one initial LLM generation was produced per task and reused across both arms. Planned episodes = 480 (two episodes per task), complete pairs = 240 (task composition: in‑distribution 144, distribution‑shift 48, adversarial 48). Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and include intent payloads, initial states, required command sequences, and preserved‑field constraints; representative task manifests and required sequences are archived and exemplify high dependency/difficulty labels ("very_hard"/"extreme").

Adapter, model, verifier, and contract: Execution used declared model gpt-5-mini and adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and was permitted up to one validator‑triggered repair per task. Critically, under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (registered in the execution contract) the paired causal contrast can only differ when the single shared candidate fails validation or when the guarded arm applies a repair. The execution manifest records maximum_model_calls = 480 and model_calls_used = 240, consistent with one initial model call per task.

Scoring and exclusions: The deterministic scorer returns a binary final outcome: safe (0) or unsafe (1) based on emulator execution and semantic invariant checks captured in validator traces. Preregistered exclusions included 'possible false‑safe' items (validator PASS but emulator unsafe outcome) and unrecoverable infra failures after allowed retries; sensitivity analyses for these channels were specified. The run experienced no infra failures and no flagged 'possible false‑safe' items; missingness and exclusions are therefore zero and archived.

Statistical analysis: The archived analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the paired contingency table, a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729), and an exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant pairs. Secondary planned outcomes (median repair counts, model‑call budgets) were recorded; repair_attempts = 0 in archived repair logs. Multiplicity control: single primary hypothesis; planned secondary tests would be FDR‑corrected when reported.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed per the preregistered plan. planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240. Provider call audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, cache_miss_count = 240, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 240, confirming exactly one shared initial generation per task. model_calls_used = 240; maximum_model_calls = 480.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency: Every paired episode was scored safe under both arms. Archived condition_summary.csv: baseline successes = 240, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 240, guarded failures = 0. Archived paired_contingency_table.csv: n11 = 240; n10 = 0; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. The paired estimate (guarded_unsafe_rate − baseline_unsafe_rate) = 0.00. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. These numeric results are identical to the archived analysis_results produced by paired_binary_analysis_v1.

Validator activity and repairs: No validator‑triggered repairs were applied (repair_attempts = 0 across repair logs). Representative validator traces (archived scoring JSONs) record validation_before and validation_after snapshots with validator fields: valid = true, violation_count = 0, violation_codes = [], and parsed_command_count/required_command_count matching the required_sequence length. Example traces show difficulty labels ("very_hard"/"extreme") and nontrivial required_command_count, yet validator PASS in each case. Deterministic_reconciliation.json records all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true.

Planned sensitivities unused: The preregistered sensitivity channels for 'possible false‑safe' flags and infra failures were unused (contamination_summary.csv is empty; missingness_summary shows zero exclusions). Subgroup slices (in‑distribution, shift, adversarial) are degenerate with zero unsafe applies in both arms and are archived for independent inspection.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded explanation for the null paired contrast: Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the adapter produced exactly one shared LLM candidate per task (provider_call_audit: shared_initial_generation = 240). The guarded arm could only differ from baseline if that shared candidate either failed deterministic validation or if a validator‑triggered repair were applied. In this execution deterministic_netops_validator_v5 validated every shared candidate (validation_after.valid = true and violation_count = 0 in archived validator traces) and repair_attempts = 0; therefore the guarded final configuration equalled the shared initial candidate for every task and no paired discordance could arise. This mechanistic account is supported by the execution_manifest, deterministic_reconciliation.json, per‑task validator traces, and the archived analysis results (estimate = 0.0, CI = [0.0, 0.0], p = 1.0).

Design tradeoffs and interpretation: The shared_initial_candidate design ensures a clean, direct pairing of the same LLM sample across arms and reduces model‑call budget (maximum_model_calls unused: 240 of 480). However, it also conditions the empirical opportunity for a verifier to change outcomes on the generator producing at least one invalid candidate. In settings where the generator is strong enough to produce validator‑passing candidates for the chosen task distribution and adversary strength, the paired contrast will be uninformative about verifier utility. Accordingly, the realized baseline unsafe rate = 0 in this run prevents detecting any verifier benefit under the registered contrast and task corpus.

Operational and experimental recommendations (artifact‑grounded): To obtain informative paired contrasts when the research goal is to estimate verifier causal effect, future designs should (1) avoid shared_initial_candidate semantics when the objective is to measure the combined causal effect of guarded generation vs unguarded generation (allow independent initial generations per arm), (2) increase repair budget (permit multiple repair iterations and instrument repair traces) so the repair policy can be exercised when validation fails, (3) increase adversary strength or use adaptive adversary protocols beyond a single fixed‑seed generator to generate more candidate failures, and (4) broaden verifier rule coverage and add cross‑checks between validator PASS and emulator outcomes to detect potential false‑safe cases. These recommendations are directly motivated by archived provider_call_audit counts (shared_initial_generation = 240), zero repair usage, and the available validator traces showing valid = true for all shared candidates.

Threats to validity and limitations (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate contract is an explicit design choice that restricts causal interpretation; archived execution manifests document contract adherence. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements a finite check set; although traces show comprehensive recording of touched fields and violation codes, uncovered semantic fault classes may remain. External validity: tasks were drawn from a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus and deterministic task generator; extrapolation to production multi‑vendor deployments requires caution. Conclusion validity: the realized baseline unsafe rate of zero undermines the power to detect verifier benefit under this design; future power planning should account for generator variability and adversary strength to ensure informative discordant pairs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, paired, emulation‑grounded evaluation of a GVR pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Observed outcome: every paired episode was safe under both arms, yielding a paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). Mechanistically, because the single shared initial candidate per task passed deterministic validation in every episode and no validator‑triggered repairs were invoked, the guarded arm could not produce discordant final outputs; the paired contrast is therefore degenerate. Our archival of preregistration, per‑call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts supports this interpretation and yields concrete, artifact‑grounded design recommendations (independent initial generations, larger repair budgets, stronger/adaptive adversaries, broader verifier coverage) for future informative GVR evaluations that seek to measure verifier causal benefits.

disclosure_statement: Models and orchestration: Execution used declared_model = gpt-5-mini via the registered adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and permitted up to one validator‑triggered repair per task. Preregistration and autonomy: the study was preregistered (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) and executed under the frozen plan after the autonomy lock. Human role and autonomy boundary: prior to the autonomy lock the human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt; all literature discovery, experiment design, preregistration, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock per the track rules. Generation semantics and contract: the registered adapter used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one shared initial generation per task reused across both arms); therefore only validator failures of the shared initial candidate or validator‑triggered repairs could create paired divergences. Execution accounting (archived): planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240; hosted_model_call_event_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240; maximum_model_calls = 480. Immutable master prompt: archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Model configuration archival: execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset) — unset temperature is recorded but does not imply determinism of the hosted provider. Reproducibility pointer: archived execution manifest, per‑call traces, task manifests, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are included in the execution bundle and are referenced in the manuscript. No manual human editing of the technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Emulator and corpus scope: tasks used a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus; external validity to production, multi‑vendor networks and operator workflows is limited.
Single model: a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) was tested; results do not imply generality across models, prompts, or prompting strategies.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired design used one shared initial generation per task; this prevents generator variability between arms and makes verifier benefit contingent on initial candidate failures.
Adversary bounds: adversarial prompts were generated under a preregistered, fixed adversary protocol and do not represent unconstrained, adaptive adversaries.

Verifier coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements a finite set of checks; uncovered semantic fault classes may remain undetected by the verifier, and verifier PASS vs simulator outcome mismatches were planned to be flagged and analyzed (none occurred in this run).
